Summary: Maintains, inspects, troubleshoots, and repairs aircraft structures, systems, engines, and components.
CredentialNotes: FAA A&P is important for civilian operators and many MRO roles; some DoD contract roles accept military technical training instead.

Summary: Installs, tests, troubleshoots, and repairs aircraft communications, navigation, electrical, and mission systems.
CredentialNotes: FCC, FAA repairman, manufacturer training, and active clearance can matter by employer and platform.

Summary: Focuses on propulsion systems, powerplant troubleshooting, inspections, removals, installations, and test-cell or field support.
CredentialNotes: A&P powerplant experience, OEM engine training, and documented military propulsion experience are useful signals.

Summary: Works on airframes, sheet metal, composite repairs, structural inspections, and corrosion control.
CredentialNotes: A&P can help; structures, sheet-metal, NDI, and depot-level repair evidence should be kept explicit.

RoleTitle: Aircraft Maintenance Quality or Production Lead
Summary: Coordinates inspection flow, quality checks, production control, and maintenance documentation across aircraft programs.
CredentialNotes: Civilian roles often value QA, CDI/CDQAR, technical inspector, maintenance control, and supervisor records.

Summary: Maintains, inspects, loads, tests, and troubleshoots aircraft weapons-release, gun, launcher, rack, and suspension systems.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, aircraft platform records, armament test-set experience, and active clearance are important signals; A&P may help only when the role is inside a civilian aircraft-maintenance organization.

Summary: Handles, inspects, assembles, stores, accounts for, and maintains ammunition, explosive ordnance, missiles, rockets, bombs, mines, torpedoes, and related support equipment.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, HAZMAT, ammunition accountability, forklift/material-handling credentials, and DoD clearance can matter by site.

Summary: Maintains shipboard gun mounts, missile launch systems, rocket or torpedo launchers, magazines, sprinklers, and ordnance support equipment.
CredentialNotes: System experience should be captured explicitly: Mk 41 VLS, Mk 45, CIWS, torpedoes, small arms, magazines, and fire-control interfaces are different employer signals.

Summary: Repairs, inspects, services, and troubleshoots small arms, crew-served weapons, towed artillery, and related mechanical weapon systems.
CredentialNotes: Factory armorer courses, depot-maintenance records, test-fire/QA experience, and technical-manual compliance are useful civilian evidence.

Summary: Manages ammunition receiving, storage, surveillance, issue, stock control, accountability, inspection, and hazardous-material handling.
CredentialNotes: Explosives safety, HAZMAT, inventory systems, QA surveillance, and ammunition handler documentation should be kept explicit.

Summary: DoD civilian ammunition-surveillance path focused on ammunition inspection, safety, reliability, lifecycle management, and explosives-safety support.
CredentialNotes: This is usually a federal civilian career path; prior ammunition surveillance, explosive safety, QA, and stockpile-management evidence matter more than OEM platform familiarity.

Summary: Tests, troubleshoots, repairs, calibrates, and supports weapon fire-control, targeting, launcher-interface, and digital artillery systems.
CredentialNotes: Electronics theory, schematic reading, test equipment, calibration, fiber-optic, laser, and secure-system experience are strong signals.

Summary: Maintains and repairs electro-optical, laser, night-vision, thermal sight, targeting, and sensor equipment tied to weapons or detection systems.
CredentialNotes: Optics handling, laser safety, alignment/calibration, electronics troubleshooting, and clearance evidence should be captured separately from generic mechanical ordnance work.

Summary: Maintains, tests, troubleshoots, and supports missile, launch, payload, guidance, checkout, and associated R&D support systems.
CredentialNotes: Clearance, nuclear surety or treaty-compliance experience, electronics test equipment, launch-system maintenance, and configuration discipline are major civilian signals.

Summary: Conducts offensive or defensive cyberspace operations, exploitation support, network operations, vulnerability analysis, and mission-focused cyber effects.
CredentialNotes: TS/SCI, polygraph, Cyber Mission Force experience, JCAC or equivalent training, scripting, and tool-development evidence are major sorting signals.

Summary: Finds, exploits, validates, and reports vulnerabilities through adversary emulation, red-team operations, and authorized penetration testing.
CredentialNotes: OSCP/GPEN/PNPT-style evidence helps commercially; cleared offensive cyber billets often value mission qualification and clearance more than public certs.

Summary: Monitors security data, triages alerts, analyzes network and endpoint events, supports incident response, and escalates threats.
CredentialNotes: Security+, CySA+, Splunk/Elastic, IDS/IPS, packet analysis, Windows/Linux, and clearance can materially change employer fit.

Summary: Proactively searches for adversary behavior across host, network, cloud, and identity telemetry using hypotheses, detections, and intelligence.
CredentialNotes: MITRE ATT&CK, SIEM/EDR, packet analysis, endpoint telemetry, scripting, and classified-network experience are key evidence.

RoleTitle: Digital Forensics and Incident Response Analyst
Summary: Investigates intrusions, analyzes endpoints and logs, preserves evidence, scopes incidents, supports containment, and writes technical findings.
CredentialNotes: GCFA/GCFE/GCIH, EDR, memory/file-system analysis, malware triage, chain of custody, and TS/SCI can matter by employer.

Summary: Analyzes malicious code, adversary tooling, exploit behavior, host artifacts, and network indicators to support detection and response.
CredentialNotes: Reverse engineering, Python, assembly, sandboxing, YARA/Sigma, and exploit-analysis evidence should be separated from generic SOC experience.

Summary: Builds and hardens secure systems, networks, cloud environments, sensors, identity controls, and defensive infrastructure.
CredentialNotes: Cloud certs, networking, Linux/Windows administration, IaC, detection engineering, and zero-trust or classified-enclave experience are important signals.

Summary: Designs, operates, secures, and troubleshoots networks, firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS, sensors, and enterprise communications infrastructure.
CredentialNotes: CCNA/CCNP, Security+, firewall/vendor training, packet analysis, and classified network operations are useful differentiators.

Summary: Plans, coordinates, documents, and synchronizes cyber operations, mission workflows, authorities, risk, and operational effects.
CredentialNotes: Planning billets value mission experience, briefing/writing, requirements translation, clearance, and operations-center exposure.

Summary: Secures space, satellite, RF, ground-station, and mission networks where cyber, communications, and space operations overlap.
CredentialNotes: Satellite communications, RF, ground systems, TS/SCI, network defense, and space-system mission context should be captured explicitly.

Summary: Plans, operates, analyzes, or supports electronic attack, electronic protection, electronic support, jamming, deception, and countermeasure missions.
CredentialNotes: Clearance, platform, spectrum tools, EA/EP/ES exposure, and specific systems such as SLQ-32 or airborne EW suites matter more than the generic EW label.

Summary: Installs, tests, troubleshoots, and supports RF receivers, transmitters, antennas, direction-finding equipment, jammers, sensors, and mission electronics.
CredentialNotes: FCC, soldering, RF test equipment, spectrum analyzer, signal generator, antenna, cabling, and clearance evidence should be captured separately.

Summary: Analyzes radar and electronic emissions, identifies emitters, maintains threat libraries, supports technical intelligence, and turns RF observations into operational findings.
CredentialNotes: Emitter identification, radar theory, ELINT databases, P-8 or shipboard collection experience, TS/SCI, and SIGINT reporting are major differentiators.

Summary: Coordinates, analyzes, and deconflicts electromagnetic spectrum use across communications, radar, satellite, cellular, GPS, and cyber-electromagnetic operations.
CredentialNotes: Joint/coalition EMSO planning, frequency management, tactical communications, GPS effects, and mission-planning tools should be documented explicitly.

Summary: Supports lab, flight, range, integration, and field testing for EW, radar, RF, avionics, countermeasure, and mission-system hardware or software.
CredentialNotes: Test equipment, data collection, troubleshooting, range operations, integration discipline, and ability to obtain a Secret or TS clearance are common gates.

Summary: Maintains, tests, troubleshoots, and supports radar surveillance, threat-warning, electronic countermeasure, and integrated avionics systems.
CredentialNotes: Radar, avionics, schematics, line-replaceable units, bench test, flightline experience, and platform type are high-signal fields.

Summary: Supports detection, tracking, jamming, fielding, training, and sustainment of counter-UAS and tactical EW systems.
CredentialNotes: Tactical EW, jamming, RF propagation, field service, sensor integration, safety, and deployed support experience are strong transition signals.

Summary: Installs, maintains, troubleshoots, and repairs electrical power, wiring, motors, controls, switchgear, and distribution systems in industrial and commercial facilities.
CredentialNotes: State electrical license or journeyman card, NFPA 70E/arc-flash, PLC and motor-control experience, and documented high-voltage work are strong civilian signals; a military electrical background often needs hours toward state licensure.

Summary: Installs, tests, and repairs shipboard electrical power, lighting, motor, and distribution systems during shipbuilding, overhaul, and repair availabilities.
CredentialNotes: Shipyard electrician experience, shipboard cable and connector standards, and prior naval electrical work are direct signals; some yards require or help toward journeyman licensure.

Summary: Maintains, troubleshoots, and repairs generators, switchgear, transfer switches, and power-distribution equipment for facilities, utilities, and standby or prime power plants.
CredentialNotes: Generator and switchgear maintenance, high-voltage, transfer-switch, and controls experience matter; utility and facilities roles may require state licensure or specific safety qualifications.

Summary: Installs, calibrates, tests, troubleshoots, and repairs commercial and industrial electronic equipment, instrumentation, controls, and communications systems.
CredentialNotes: Electronics theory, schematic reading, test equipment, calibration, PLC and instrumentation work, and shipboard or industrial electronics experience are strong signals; a clearance can matter for defense-electronics employers.

Summary: Operates, tests, calibrates, troubleshoots, and maintains sonar, underwater surveillance, acoustic collection, and associated combat-system electronics.
CredentialNotes: Specific platform and system history matters: surface, submarine, SURTASS, hull array, towed array, combat-control test equipment, schematics, calibration, and clearance should be captured explicitly.

Summary: Analyzes active and passive sonar returns, acoustic signatures, broadband/narrowband data, contact behavior, and environmental factors to support undersea detection and classification.
CredentialNotes: ACINT, broadband/narrowband analysis, contact classification, acoustic signature work, submarine operations, and TS/SCI evidence are stronger signals than a generic sonar title.

Summary: Supports anti-submarine warfare analysis, target localization, contact evaluation, threat recognition, tactical recommendations, and ASW mission support.
CredentialNotes: Surface/submarine platform, ASW operator/supervisor qualifications, acoustic analysis, target motion, fire-control integration, and clearance are key differentiators.

Summary: Supports sonar, underwater communications, undersea sensors, hydrophone arrays, acoustic data collection, combat systems, and submarine or surface ASW mission systems.
CredentialNotes: Undersea system roles often split between operator SME, field service, integration/test, and engineering-support tracks; degree requirements should be treated separately.

Summary: Supports lab, pier-side, shipboard, submarine, range, at-sea, and acoustic test events for sonar, sensors, underwater communications, and combat-system hardware or software.
CredentialNotes: At-sea test support, acoustic data collection, system calibration, troubleshooting, test equipment, and ability to work around classified systems are high-signal fields.

Summary: Solicits, negotiates, awards, administers, and closes out federal contracts for supplies and services, including price and cost analysis and Federal Acquisition Regulation compliance.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-1102 series; DAWIA / FAC-C contracting certification and a contracting-officer warrant govern signature authority.

Summary: Analyzes and coordinates a supply chain across its life cycle: acquisition, distribution, allocation, maintenance planning, and disposition of materiel and parts.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-0346 series; DAWIA life-cycle-logistics and APICS/DoD logistics credentials are valued.

Summary: Studies organizational procedures, manpower, and programs and recommends efficiency and process improvements; the civilian analog to program and manpower analysis.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-0343 series; program-management (PMP / DAWIA PM) credentials help for higher-graded analyst roles.

Summary: Conducts budget, cost, and financial analysis to inform resourcing and investment decisions.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-0501 series; CDFM/CGFM and DAWIA business-financial-management credentials are valued.

Summary: Develops and administers physical, personnel, and information security programs, access control, and the safeguarding of assets and facilities.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-0080 series; industrial-security (NISP), physical-security, and clearance-adjudication training are high-signal.

Summary: Administers recruitment, staffing, classification, benefits, and employee and labor relations programs.
CredentialNotes: Federal GS-0201 series; SHRM/HRCI certifications and federal Delegated Examining training are valued.

Summary: Performs general business, program, and industrial-operations support spanning procurement, planning, analysis, and administration without a single specialized track.
CredentialNotes: Broad federal GS-0301 / GS-1101 destination; project/program-management credentials help but no single license defines it.
